title: Doxygen documentation portal is live
content: The Heretical Documentation portal is now live. It brings selected workspace and product documentation together without moving that material out of its owning repositories. This is deployed development infrastructure, not a product release: no engine, framework, editor, or library release is implied. What was built The portal has its own source repository, Heretical-Solutions/Heretical-Documentation, and builds with Doxygen 1.18.0 and Doxygen Awesome CSS 2.5.0. Both the generator release and theme revision are pinned and verified. Doxygen is restored for the build rather than installed globally or committed as a binary; the theme is restored from a locked Git commit. Authoritative eng/ commands cover restore, build, local preview, and validation. The build aggregates explicitly selected Markdown documents into ignored intermediates, preserves relative links and media, and records source provenance. Canonical documentation stays in its original repository. The current publication includes workspace architecture, policies, repository records, and the blog’s product guides. It does not invent API sections for products that publish no library API. Source and integration Superproject PR #7 registered the portal as an independent submodule. The final publication used these exact source revisions: Input Revision Superproject develop 5fb634ba67d674994e734be031191ac6f7824be5 Portal master e02da8b27803a4c172a6928bf13976241bdf9c8e Blog master 1c505359e5b4afb9323906b4b4589b00e676f57f The generated source provenance page records the inputs for the published site. Source aggregation, portal registration, and website deployment remain separate operations with separate review gates. Validation and publication The portal passed local validation, a clean canonical recursive checkout, and its GitHub Actions build. Checks covered source and tool pins, internal links and fragments, document coverage, navigation assets, payload hygiene, and the project Pages base path. A separate C# extraction fixture passed without Unity, .asmdef resolution, generated project files, compilation, or stubs. That fixture demonstrates source extraction only; it does not prove Unity compatibility, compilation, or runtime behavior. Final workflow run #3 restored the selected inputs, validated the site, uploaded the Pages artifact, and deployed it successfully. The live catalog, blog guides, search resources, and required license texts were checked, and desktop and mobile Firefox renders were inspected. The mobile layout collapses the documentation tree behind a navigation control while keeping search and the light/dark control available. Boundaries and remaining checks The portal deploys through its own GitHub Actions workflow to GitHub project Pages. The blog keeps its separate repository, manual editorial process, and gh-pages publication history. Neither site uses a custom domain in this phase. Because the canonical superproject is private, full CI source restore uses a narrowly scoped read-only credential; untrusted pull requests receive no source credential and run structural checks only. The initial supported build host is Linux x86_64. No versioned documentation, product API reference, or release compatibility claim has been added. Interactive search, theme-toggle, and browser-console review remain manual acceptance checks. Future product sections will come from real registered repositories and their own canonical documentation.

title: Blog repository initialised
content: The development blog now exists as its own first-party repository, Heretical-Solutions/Heretical-Blog, with its source checked out in the workspace at sites/blog/. Superproject registration is a separate later step. This post records what was set up; it makes no claim about any product being released. What is in place A Jekyll site using the Chirpy theme consumed as a packaged gem, pinned by a committed Gemfile.lock. Site identity, UTC dates, search, categories, tags, Atom feed, syntax highlighting, and responsive light/dark mode. Comments, analytics, and PWA/offline caching are disabled. Authoritative commands under eng/ for dependency restore, a local preview server, a production build into the ignored artifacts/site/ directory, and validation. Product documentation for requirements, build, quick start, editorial process, deployment, and compatibility. Publication model for now Publication is deliberately manual. Approved source is committed to master, built and validated locally, then published as a deployment-only gh-pages branch for GitHub project Pages at /Heretical-Blog/. Generated HTML never lands on master, and each deployment commit records the source revision it came from. Superproject registration is reviewed separately from product publication. There are no GitHub Actions workflows, repository webhooks, or automatic draft generation in this initial phase. Build/deploy automation and event-driven editorial drafts are separate later proposals, each with its own approval gate. Editorial process _drafts/ is the single draft queue. A human reviewer promotes approved content into _posts/, and production builds exclude drafts, so unreviewed material cannot reach the published site.
